questions.text: Why are these temperate grasslands called the 'Breadbasket of the World,' and what agricultural conditions favor wheat and maize production here?.
questions.text_as_printed: Why are these temperate grasslands called the 'Breadbasket of the World,' and what agricultural conditions favor wheat and maize production here?. (Average )

answer.value: The central plains are called the Great Plains of the Prairies, which are found between the Appalachians to the east and the mountains to the west. These plains are very extensive (3/5 percent of the total land area of North America) and have a frontage ranging from flat to sloping. These plains are formed by the Mississippi and Missouri rivers and their tributaries, making them one of the most fertile plains in the world and a good agricultural area.

questions.text: Write about the major lakes of the North American continent.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the major lakes of the North American continent. (Average )

answer.value: North America has a large number of freshwater and saltwater lakes, most of which are located along the southern edge of the Canadian Plateau. The major lakes are Huron, Ontario, Michigan, Erie, and Superior. Collectively, the lakes are called the Great Lakes. Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes and the largest freshwater lake in the world. The cities of Chicago and Detroit are located on the shores of the lake, and all of these lakes provide important waterways.

questions.text: Write about the population density of the North American continent.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the population density of the North American continent. (Average )

answer.value: The highest population density is found in the eastern parts of North America, where there is a lot of urbanization, for example, New York, Washington, Chicago, etc., but most of the northern part of the continent is generally empty due to the high snow cover. The urban centers and industrial areas of the United States are the areas of highest population density, with 98% of the population of North America being urban.
